title: Things to Do in Podgora, Croatia: Top Attractions 2027
metaDescription: Top things to do in Podgora, Croatia in 2027: the Seagull Wings monument, main beach, promenade, diving, water sports, olive oil tasting, with prices.
content:
## What Are the Top Attractions in Podgora?

Podgora is a small town on the Makarska Riviera, about 9 km northwest of Makarska and roughly an hour's drive southeast of Split. It sits between the sea and the steep Biokovo mountain slopes. Its main draws are one large monument, a long stretch of pebble coast, a flat waterfront walk and a handful of active options. The town has no major museum or fortress, so the visit is built around the sea. The list below covers the headline sights and activities. Prices are typical summer figures and change by year and operator.

## Seagull Wings Monument (Krila Galeba)

The Seagull Wings monument is the landmark of Podgora. It is a large concrete sculpture of two upswept wings, visible from the town and from boats along the coast. It was made by the Croatian sculptor Dušan Džamonja and commemorates the Battle of Podgora in 1942, when partisan fighters clashed with Italian forces here. The monument stands on a rise above the centre, and the walk up takes about 15–20 minutes at an easy pace. Entry is free and there is no ticket office.

The site is open at all hours. Go in the early evening, when the heat drops and the light over the water turns warm. The viewpoint gives a wide look over the town, the coast and the islands of Brač and Hvar on clear days. Wear proper shoes, since the final approach has uneven ground and little shade. Bring water in July and August.

## Podgora Town Beach

The central beach is the largest in Podgora and the most convenient. It is a pebble beach with a gradual entry into clear water. Facilities include showers, changing cabins, lifeguards, and sun loungers and umbrellas for hire. Cafes and restaurants sit directly behind it. The beach has an access ramp and a sea lift for swimmers with reduced mobility, which is uncommon on this coast.

Expect to pay about €10–€15 for a pair of loungers with an umbrella in peak season. Spreading a towel on a free section of the pebbles costs nothing. Water shoes are worth buying, as the pebbles are comfortable to walk on but sharper near the rock edges.

The beach is busiest from 11:00 to 16:00. Swim before 09:30 or after 17:00 for calmer water and more space.

## Plišivac Beach

Plišivac lies north of the centre and is backed by pine forest. The water is among the clearest on this section of the coast, and the pines give natural shade without paying for an umbrella. It is quieter than the town beach, which makes it the better pick for families with young swimmers who want space. It is a short walk or a quick bike ride from the centre along the coastal path.

Bring drinks and snacks, as services are thinner here than in town. Arrive before 10:00 in July and August to get a shaded spot under the trees.

## Seafront Promenade and Harbour

The waterfront path runs along the coast and links the beaches, the harbour, cafes and restaurants. It is flat, mostly paved and suitable for strollers. The harbour is where fishing boats and excursion boats dock, so late afternoon brings some activity. A walk from one end of the town centre to the other takes about 30 minutes.

The promenade is at its best at sunset. Most restaurants here put tables at the water's edge. A main course in a harbour restaurant usually costs €14–€25 for fish or meat, and grilled fresh fish is sold by weight, often €55–€80 per kg. Check the weight and price before ordering whole fish.

## Diving in Podgora

The local dive club, Birgmajer-Sub, runs diving from town. It offers guided dives for certified divers, equipment hire and courses for beginners. Water temperature is around 24–25 °C at the surface in August and 15–17 °C in May. The best visibility comes in late spring and autumn, when fewer swimmers and boats stir the water. A guided single dive typically costs €40–€60 with gear, and an introductory try-dive costs more than a standard certified dive. Book at least a day ahead in summer.

## Water Sports and Boat or Bike Rental

The main beach is the base for banana boat rides, jet skis and boat hire. A banana boat ride typically costs about €10–€15 per person for a short run. Jet skis are priced per 15 or 30 minutes and cost much more per person. The rental agency Podgora Puls hires out bikes and boats.

A small boat rented for a few hours costs less than most guided boat tours when split between four people. Check the licence rules first: many small motorboats need no licence below a set engine power, and larger ones do. A bike is the easiest way to reach Plišivac and the northern coast without a car.

The jet ski is usually poor value here. A short ride costs far more than other activities in this guide and gives you a few minutes on the water. A boat rental gives you hours.

## Olive Oil Tasting

Olive oil is a local product, and Uljara & Kusaonica Acinger offers tasting of the local oil. Plan on a short visit of 30–45 minutes. Bottles of local extra virgin oil usually cost about €12–€20 for 0.5 l. Buy directly from the producer rather than from tourist shops on the front, which sell mixed or imported oils at higher prices. Ask for the harvest year: fresher oil from the latest harvest has a sharper, peppery taste.

## Churches and Old Podgora

Podgora has several churches and chapels, many small and tied to older village life or to the sea. They are free to view from outside, and many are open for services only. A short walk through the old part of town above the waterfront takes in several. Dress with covered shoulders and knees if you plan to enter.

## Best Time to Visit

July and August bring the warmest sea, about 24–26 °C, and the highest prices and crowds. June and September are the best balance: sea temperatures remain near 22–24 °C, beaches have space and accommodation is cheaper. Late May and early October suit walking, diving and quiet evenings, though some beach bars and rental points close or reduce hours.

## Local Tips

- Walk to the Seagull Wings in the evening and take a head torch or phone light for the descent after sunset.
- Buy a pair of water shoes before arriving; shops in town charge more than home stores.
- Carry some cash. Small beach services, cafes and producers do not always accept cards.
- Ask your accommodation for the free tourist-board map. It shows the promenade, beaches and walking routes.
- Put the best stretch of the day into the beach: swim early, spend midday in shade or at a restaurant, then walk the promenade in the evening.

## Getting Around Podgora

The town centre is compact and walkable. The main beach, harbour, restaurants and most accommodation sit within about 1 km of each other. A bike covers Plišivac and the hillside monument faster. The nearest large town for supplies and bus connections is Makarska, a short bus or taxi ride away. Parking in town fills early in July and August, so leave the car at your accommodation when possible.

faq.question: What is the most famous attraction in Podgora?
faq.answer: The Seagull Wings monument is the best-known landmark in Podgora. It is a concrete sculpture by Dušan Džamonja that commemorates the 1942 Battle of Podgora. Entry is free and it is open at all hours.

faq.question: Is Podgora worth visiting?
faq.answer: Yes, for beach and relaxed seaside stays. Podgora has a long pebble coast, clear water, a flat promenade and quieter beaches than nearby Makarska. It is less suited to travellers who want museums, nightlife or historic sights.

faq.question: How much does a beach lounger cost in Podgora?
faq.answer: A pair of loungers with an umbrella usually costs about €10–€15 in peak summer. Prices are lower in June and September. Free pebble space is available on every beach.

faq.question: Can you dive in Podgora?
faq.answer: Yes. The local club Birgmajer-Sub offers guided dives, equipment hire and courses. A guided dive typically costs €40–€60 including gear, and booking a day ahead in summer is advised.

faq.question: What is the best beach in Podgora?
faq.answer: The central town beach is best for convenience, with loungers, showers, lifeguards, cafes and an access ramp. Plišivac, north of the centre, is the better choice for pine shade and a quieter setting.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Podgora?
faq.answer: June and September offer the best mix of warm sea (22–24 °C), lower prices and fewer people. July and August are warmest but busiest and most expensive. Late May and early October suit diving and walking.

faq.question: Is Podgora good for families?
faq.answer: Yes. The gradual pebble entry, lifeguards, showers, flat promenade and many cafes make it practical with children. Quieter Plišivac suits families who prefer more space.

quickAnswer: The top things to do in Podgora are the Seagull Wings monument above the town, Podgora's central pebble beach, the seafront promenade, Plišivac beach under the pines, diving with a local club, water sports, and olive oil tasting. Most sights are free. Beach loungers and activities cost roughly €5–€60.
